title: Node inference credential: restricted inference key, fail-closed on revoke
reasoning: Hermes runs in a bunker and its gateway answers over the tailnet, but a turn dies at 'agent init failed: No inference provider configured'. The inference gateway is reachable from a node, while the routing proxy and resolve API bind loopback only. The sanctioned pattern is a revocable restricted key (accessRestricted + accessAllow, enforced before credential lookup), never an operator key on a remote box.

The node's ~/.hermes/.env carries it, mode 600, never in argv or a log. 3. prompt.submit through the node gateway returns a completion, with requested vs served model recorded. 4. Revoking the key fails closed with a readable error, proven live. 5. No operator credential is copied to any agent; blast radius stated in specs/HARNESS.md.

title: Node sizing and disk policy: refuse admission with the number
reasoning: Measured: 4.3 GB free inside an agent on a host at 97%, while one repo node costs ~1.5 GB and sibling agents swing free space by 5 GB. Without a policy nodes fill the host and fail mid-job, which is the orphaned-work failure this fleet has already had.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A documented floor per node role, justified by measured footprint. 2. The ladder refuses admission below the floor, naming the number, before any install begins. 3. A reclaim step (build cache, job dirs, stale clones) runs before refusal. 4. A boundary test proves the refusal fires. 5. bunker status residue (orphan homes/keys/users) is reaped and reported.

title: Node lifecycle: supervisor, renew, destroy/rebuild
reasoning: A node's gateway is started with nohup and dies on agent stop/renew; agent TTL is 4h unless renewed. A node that silently disappears is indistinguishable from a node that failed, and cancellation is only possible by killing the process group from a second exec (client kill and --timeout do NOT stop remote work).
acceptance_criteria: 1. The harness runs under a supervisor that restarts it and records restarts. 2. Agent TTL is renewed automatically while the node is active. 3. Cancelling a dispatch kills the process GROUP and the evidence shows it (job pid/pgid written by the job, killed, completion artifact absent after the deadline). 4. destroy then create reproduces the node from recorded commands with no manual step. 5. A node that dies mid-job causes redelivery, and idempotency prevents duplicated work.

title: P4 — GitReins guard refuses every documentation-only commit as DEGRADED PASS (lint scope is Python-only)
reasoning:
The GitReins guard cannot pass a documentation-only commit in this repo. `.gitreins/config.yaml`
sets `guards.allow_skips: false` and `lint_command: bash -n $(git ls-files "*.sh")`, but the lint
guard decides its scope from staged file extensions and reports `skip_reason=no staged files`
whenever no Python file is staged, which makes Tier 1 `DEGRADED PASS`; the repo policy then refuses
the commit and no commit object is created.

Measured 2026-10-30 on a docs-only change (README.md + docs/audits/*.md + board events.jsonl) from
worktree `~/worktrees/code-factory-readme-20261030-182833`, tip cc0a1e4:

- `git commit -F msg` -> guard log `.gitreins/logs/guard-20261030T212945.104300Z.log`
- `overall: PASS (DEGRADED — skipped checks)`, `guards: 3 (0 failed, 1 skipped)`,
  `skipped_steps: - lint: no staged files`, detail line `No Python files staged`
- `secrets` PASS (gitleaks clean), `tests (full)` PASS (exit 0, `SELFTEST: PASS`, which runs
  `bash -n` over every script internally)
- `git log --oneline -1` after the attempt still shows the pre-commit tip: no commit was created

The consequence is that every docs and readme lane change, and every board-only commit, needs a
hook bypass to land. That is exactly the kind of skip the repo's own gate is meant to refuse, so
the gate must be able to grade a non-Python diff instead of skipping it.

Acceptance criteria:

1. A documentation-only commit (no .py and no .sh changed) completes through the guard with Tier 1
   `PASS`, not `DEGRADED PASS`, from a clean worktree of this repo; a re-runnable reproduction is
   `git commit --allow-empty -m probe` on a scratch branch with a README line added.
2. The guard log for that run shows the lint gate executed rather than skipped, and names what it
   executed (`bash -n` targets or an explicit "no lint targets in this diff" that the repo policy
   accepts).
3. No bypass (`--no-verify`, `core.hooksPath=/dev/null`) is used in the reproduction, and the
   resulting commit exists on the branch.
4. `bash tests/selftest.sh` still passes and the guard's secrets and full-test legs still run.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A documentation-only commit completes through the guard with Tier 1 PASS, not DEGRADED PASS, from a clean worktree.
2. The guard log shows the lint gate executed and names its targets instead of skipping.
3. No bypass (--no-verify, core.hooksPath=/dev/null) is used and the commit exists on the branch.
4. bash tests/selftest.sh still passes and the secrets and full-test legs still run.
foreman_note: Root cause measured 2026-10-30 in gitreins 0.17.1: engine/guard_manager.py::_check_lint builds py_files from changed_files filtered to '*.py' and never reads guards.lint_command; with no staged .py it returns GuardResult(skipped=True, skip_reason='no staged files'). Experiment in this repo's worktree: staging any *.py makes the identical tree return Tier 1 PASS with 'lint — ok'; staging none (every docs/README/board/shell-only commit) returns DEGRADED PASS and, with allow_skips:false, the commit is refused. So the blast radius is every non-Python commit in this repo, not documentation only. grade_full_tree exists but is CLI-only (gitreins guard --full), there is no config key; repo-side options are (a) allow_skips:true — weakens the gate, (b) invoke the hook as 'gitreins guard --full' so lint grades the tree's four .py files and names them — no weakening, local hook change, not shippable in-repo, (c) upstream: make the lint lane honour lint_command or accept a non-.py scope.
